title: Activation & Scope-Mapping Workshop: Hybrid POC
objectives:
1) Rapidly align internal and customer stakeholders on POC goals and success criteria.
2) Map functional scope across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployment options.
3) Produce a timeboxed activation plan and identified blockers for the first 4 weeks.
prework: Customer to share current API traffic profile (sample traces + qps by endpoint)
Customer to provide a short list of 3 representative prompts / input types
Redwood to provision demo tenant and share test API key (read-only) before session
Attendees to review Hybrid POC one-pager (linked in artifacts)
agenda: 00:10 - 00:25: Customer context: product flows, constraints, and regulatory notes (customer)
00:25 - 00:40: Traffic & quality objectives mapping — what matters for first release (group)
00:40 - 01:10: Technical deep-dive: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private — tradeoffs and templates (Redwood)
01:10 - 01:35: Breakout A: Data, security, and compliance mapping (customer + Sasha)
01:35 - 02:00: Breakout B: Latency/throughput constraints and routing policy choices (customer + Liam)
02:00 - 02:20: Report back: scope decisions and outstanding unknowns (each breakout)
02:20 - 02:40: Define MVP POC scope, acceptance criteria, and success metrics (group)
02:40 - 02:55: Activation plan: roles, milestones for first 4 weeks, and demo date (facilitator)
02:55 - 03:00: Next steps, action owners, risks, and meeting close
slide_outline: Customer context: product, users, and constraints (1 slide)
Redwood deployment options overview: quick comparison table (hosted / dedicated / private)
Security & data flow: where data lives and encryption/KMS notes
Quantization / model variant recommendations by workload
Ops and observability: console dashboards and rollout controls
Proposed MVP POC scope & acceptance checklist
Known risks, open questions, and mitigation proposals
Action owners and next meeting agenda
facilitation_notes: Keep the session outcome-focused: the objective is not to design the final architecture, but to leave with a concrete MVP scope and activation plan. Use parking-lot for deep technical debates and capture owners. For each breakout, set a single question to answer (e.g., "Which data can remain in-hosted mode vs must stay on-prem?") and one deliverable (a 3-line summary). Use live whiteboard for traffic shapes and routing diagrams. If the customer pushes for full on-prem timeline, reframe to a phased POC: (1) Hosted evaluation, (2) Dedicated performance test, (3) Private pilot for regulated flows.
materials: Pre-provisioned demo tenant and sample API key
Slide deck (this outline) + two appendix slides with config templates
Traffic sample CSV and prompt set (provided by customer)
expected_outcomes: Agreed MVP scope for the POC (features + traffic envelope)
Clear acceptance criteria (latency, cost estimates, quality checks)
Activation plan with owners and milestones for weeks 0-4
List of blockers (integration, security signoffs) and mitigation owners
follow_up_actions: Redwood: Share finalized slide deck and 4-week swimlane by EOD +1 (owner: Maya)
Customer: Deliver masked traffic traces and credentials for non-prod cluster (owner: Samira)
Infra: Configure dedicated test pool based on agreed qps targets (owner: Liam)
Security: Submit privacy/data-flow diagram to customer security for signoff (owner: Sasha)
SE: Create monitoring eval prompts and register in Redwood Optimize (owner: Diego)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customer cannot share realistic traffic traces — Mitigation: use synthetic workload generator and schedule a shadow test
Risk: Private deployment signoff delayed — Mitigation: prepare a parallel Dedicated-based test with same acceptance criteria
Risk: Latency targets unattainable under current budget — Mitigation: propose staged optimization (batching + quantized model) and re-baseline after week 2
